speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; since infants cannot speak, I will rely on your observations to guide our examination. Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes, such as whether the sounds occur only when feeding, crying, or breathing normally?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Tracheomalacia. The clinical picture of stridor and wheezing that worsens with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, accompanied by post-prandial vomiting, is highly characteristic of tracheomalacia. Would you like me to request a neck flexion X-ray or an upper airway study to confirm this?
